newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland cuts minimum fixed bond prices.
newsitem.headline: Poland cuts minimum fixed bond prices.

text.p: The Polish treasury cut the minimum price of its 15-percent two year bonds to 89.82 from 90.21 at the last auction on March 5, 1997, the National Bank of Poland said.
It has also said the minimum price of 12-percent five year bonds fell to 79.29 from 79.41.
The average prices fell to 90.13 on the shorter paper and 79.38 on the longer bonds from the previous 90.40 and 79.47 respectively.
The finance ministry sold a total of 125 million zlotys worth of the bonds after investors bid for 161 million against the joint Treasury's 800 million zloty offer.
